name: Hacker, pack your bags!
description: It's well known that the best way to distract from something is to do one's favourite thing. Job is such a thing for Leha. So the hacker began to work hard in order to get rid of boredom. It means that Leha began to hack computers all over the world. For such zeal boss gave the hacker a vacation of exactly x days. You know the majority of people prefer to go somewhere for a vacation, so Leha immediately went to the travel agency. There he found out that n vouchers left. i -th voucher is characterized by three integers l i , r i , cost i — day of departure from Vičkopolis, day of arriving back in Vičkopolis and cost of the voucher correspondingly. The duration of the i -th voucher is a value r i - l i + 1 . At the same time Leha wants to split his own vocation into two parts. Besides he wants to spend as little money as possible. Formally Leha wants to choose exactly two vouchers i and j ( i ≠ j ) so that they don't intersect, sum of their durations is exactly x and their total cost is as minimal as possible. Two vouchers i and j don't intersect if only at least one of the following conditions is fulfilled: r i < l j or r j < l i . Help Leha to choose the necessary vouchers!
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n and x (2 ≤ n , x ≤ 2·10 5 ) — the number of vouchers in the travel agency and the duration of Leha's vacation correspondingly. Each of the next n lines contains three integers l i , r i and cost i (1 ≤ l i ≤ r i ≤ 2·10 5 , 1 ≤ cost i ≤ 10 9 ) — description of the voucher.
output_specification: Print a single integer — a minimal amount of money that Leha will spend, or print - 1 if it's impossible to choose two disjoint vouchers with the total duration exactly x .
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 822C — Hacker, pack your bags! [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
